questions.retry_hint: THAN sets this year's lesson against LAST YEAR'S VERSION - two things - and the adjective is long. Ask: does a long adjective ever take -er? 'The most' would be for a whole group of lessons, not for a pair.

questions.stem: The student ________ her password when the school's online system sent her a security alert.
questions.trap_type: 'The system sent a security alert' = sudden event. The student was already in the middle of changing = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The system SENT an alert = sudden past event. The student was already changing her password = WAS CHANGING (past continuous). Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing.
questions.retry_hint: The system SENT HER A SECURITY ALERT - a sudden event that cut in. Ask: which choice shows an action already under way in the PAST? She had not finished the job when the alert arrived on her screen.

questions.stem: There was ________ guidance about online safety in the school handbook — students had to search for information themselves.
questions.trap_type: 'Guidance' is uncountable → use LITTLE. 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' are for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: LITTLE + uncountable noun. Guidance = uncountable → LITTLE guidance. 'Few guidance' is WRONG — you cannot count pieces of guidance. LITTLE = not much (uncountable).
questions.retry_hint: GUIDANCE is uncountable - you cannot say 'one guidance, two guidances'. Ask: which choice partners an uncountable noun to mean 'not much'? 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' all need things you can count.

questions.stem: Protecting your personal information online is extremely important, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive present simple ('is') → negative question tag. 'Is' → isn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive present 'to be' → negative tag. Protecting information IS important, ISN'T it? POSITIVE → NEGATIVE tag. IS → ISN'T.
questions.retry_hint: PROTECTING YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION - the statement is positive, and its verb is a present form of 'to be'. Ask: does the tag echo the verb already there, or borrow 'does'? After a positive statement, which way does the tag turn?

questions.stem: The cyberbullying complaint ________ by the school counsellor before any action was taken.
questions.trap_type: The complaint received the action. Past passive: was/were + past participle.
questions.learning_tip: WAS/WERE + past participle = passive! The complaint WAS INVESTIGATED = the counsellor investigated it; complaint received the action. NEVER 'was being investigated' (P5 level).
questions.retry_hint: The COMPLAINT could not look into itself: THE SCHOOL COUNSELLOR did that, before any action followed. Ask: which choice is passive (the subject receives the action) and set in the past? One complaint, so pick the singular helper.

questions.stem: The teacher asked students ________ their devices during the assembly.
questions.trap_type: Negative reported speech: told/asked + object + not to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: ASKED someone NOT TO + base verb. The teacher asked students NOT TO USE their devices. Formula: asked + person + not to + verb (base form).
questions.retry_hint: ASKED STUDENTS = a reported command, and it is a ban DURING THE ASSEMBLY. Ask: after 'asked + person', does the little word 'not' come before 'to' or after it? Whatever you choose, the verb that follows stays in its plain form.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Adverbs of manner)

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Read all messages (1)________ before clicking any link, especially from unknown senders.' Signal: doing something with care and attention = CAREFULLY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'slowly' (not in the box) or 'fast'. The point is attention, not speed: an unknown sender is a risk.
questions.learning_tip: CAREFULLY = with full attention, taking no risks. Read CAREFULLY before you click on anything.
questions.retry_hint: You must check EVERY MESSAGE BEFORE YOU CLICK ON ANY LINK, especially if THE SENDER IS A STRANGER. Ask: which box adverb means 'with full attention, taking no risks'? Speed is not the issue here; attention is.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'If you receive a suspicious message, (2)________ close the window and tell a trusted adult.' Signal: doing something immediately and without delay = QUICKLY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'fast'. The dash spells out the meaning: DO NOT WAIT EVEN A SECOND - this is about how SOON you act, not how fast you move.
questions.learning_tip: IMMEDIATELY = right now, with no delay. Compare FAST, which is about the speed of a movement, not the moment it starts.
questions.retry_hint: The dash orders it: DO NOT WAIT EVEN A SECOND. Ask: which box adverb means 'right now, with no delay'? A word about high speed would describe how quickly you move, not how soon you begin.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Cyberbullying can happen (3)________ — victims may suffer without anyone around them knowing.' Signal: without noise or visible action, undetected = SILENTLY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'quietly' (not in the box). Victims suffer for months without anyone else noticing - no sound, no sign.
questions.learning_tip: SILENTLY = making no sound and leaving no sign. Cyberbullying can go on SILENTLY for months.
questions.retry_hint: VICTIMS MAY SUFFER FOR MONTHS WITHOUT ANYONE ELSE NOTICING - not a sound, not a sign. Ask: which box adverb means 'making no noise and leaving no trace'? Match the adverb to the hidden suffering.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Students who understand online safety usually perform (4)________ when asked to identify suspicious websites.' Signal: in a good and skilled manner = WELL (adverb form of 'good').
questions.trap_type: Students write 'good' (an adjective, not in the box). The blank follows the verb 'perform', and the clue is 'scoring high marks'.
questions.learning_tip: WELL = the adverb partner of 'good'. They perform WELL. Never 'perform good' - a verb needs an adverb.
questions.retry_hint: The pupils are SCORING HIGH MARKS in the CYBER QUIZ, so they perform to a high standard. Ask: which box adverb is the partner of the adjective 'good'? Remember that 'good' itself can never follow the verb 'perform'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Developers work (5)________ to create firewalls that block harmful content from reaching young users.' Signal: with great effort and energy = HARD (adverb). HARD ≠ HARDLY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'hardly', which means almost not at all - the exact opposite. The engineers stay late into the night.
questions.learning_tip: HARD (adverb) = with great effort. Work HARD. HARDLY = almost not at all. One letter changes everything.
questions.retry_hint: The engineers stay OFTEN LATE INTO THE NIGHT to build firewalls. Ask: which box adverb means 'with great effort'? Careful - adding -ly to it would flip the meaning to 'almost not at all', the exact opposite.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Online misinformation spreads (6)________ — a false story can reach millions of people within hours.' Signal: moving or happening with great speed = FAST.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'immediately'. The clue is speed of travel: a made-up story can race around the world within hours.
questions.learning_tip: FAST (adverb) = at great speed, and it never takes -ly. News spreads FAST. IMMEDIATELY answers 'how soon', FAST answers 'how quickly'.
questions.retry_hint: A MADE-UP STORY CAN RACE AROUND THE WORLD WITHIN HOURS. Ask: which box adverb describes great speed and never takes an -ly ending? The adverb meaning 'with no delay' has already been used for closing the window.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Children who learn safe online habits from an early age use the internet (7)________ and responsibly as they grow older.' Signal: in a content and positive way = HAPPILY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'well'. The clue is 'enjoying it without fear or worry' - a feeling, not a skill level.
questions.learning_tip: HAPPILY = in a cheerful, contented way. Children who feel safe use the internet HAPPILY.
questions.retry_hint: The children are ENJOYING it WITHOUT FEAR OR WORRY as they grow older. Ask: which box adverb describes a cheerful, contented feeling while doing something? The others describe speed, effort, silence or care.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'When correcting a friend who has shared false information online, do it (8)________ so they do not feel embarrassed.' Signal: with care not to cause pain or embarrassment = GENTLY.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'carefully'. The aim is that nobody feels embarrassed - the correction must be soft and kind.
questions.learning_tip: GENTLY = in a soft, kind way that does not hurt anyone's feelings. Correct a friend GENTLY.
questions.retry_hint: You are correcting A FRIEND, and the aim is SO THAT NOBODY FEELS EMBARRASSED. Ask: which box adverb means 'in a soft, kind way that does not hurt'? Speed and effort have nothing to do with it.

C.passage: Using the internet safely takes good habits. Read every message (1)________ before you click on any link, especially if the sender is a stranger. If a message looks suspicious, (2)________ close the window - do not wait even a second - and tell a trusted adult. Cyberbullying can happen (3)________: victims may suffer for months without anyone else noticing. Pupils who understand online safety usually perform (4)________ in the school's cyber quiz, scoring high marks. Software engineers work (5)________, often late into the night, to build firewalls that block harmful content. False news spreads (6)________: a made-up story can race around the world within hours. Children who learn safe habits early use the internet (7)________, enjoying it without fear or worry. When you correct a friend who has shared a false story, do it (8)________ so that nobody feels embarrassed.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Cyber wellness means using technology safely and responsibly. One of the first steps is to create a strong (1)________ for every online account — it should include letters, numbers and symbols. Managing (2)________ is equally important: too many hours on screens can affect your sleep and mood. Some people use the internet to harm others. A (3)________ is someone who hurts or threatens another person online, often hiding behind an (4)________ identity with no real name. Living well in the (5)________ age means knowing how to enjoy technology and when to put it down.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'for every online account, at least eight characters long, includes letters, numbers and symbols' = password.
questions.learning_tip: A PASSWORD = a secret combination of characters used to access an online account. A strong PASSWORD is long and hard for others to guess.
questions.retry_hint: It must include LETTERS, NUMBERS AND SYMBOLS, and every ONLINE ACCOUNT needs a STRONG one. Ask: which box word names the secret code you type to prove that the account is yours? It is a thing, not a person.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'hours looking at a phone or computer screen — affects sleep, eyesight and mood' = screen time.
questions.learning_tip: SCREEN TIME = the amount of time a person spends looking at a digital screen. Managing SCREEN TIME = controlling how long you use devices each day.
questions.retry_hint: TOO MANY HOURS ON SCREENS CAN AFFECT YOUR SLEEP AND MOOD, so it must be MANAGED. Ask: which box entry names the number of hours a person spends looking at a device each day? It is written as two words, not one.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'uses online platforms to hurt, threaten or embarrass another person' = cyberbully.
questions.learning_tip: A CYBERBULLY = a person who uses the internet to hurt, threaten or embarrass someone else. CYBER = online; BULLY = someone who harms others deliberately.
questions.retry_hint: The blank follows 'A', and the person described HURTS OR THREATENS ANOTHER PERSON ONLINE. Ask: which box entry names that kind of person? The others name a secret code, a number of hours, or a hidden identity.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'hiding behind an ___ identity — does not reveal their real name' = anonymous.
questions.learning_tip: ANONYMOUS = not revealing one's name or identity. Cyberbullies sometimes act behind an ANONYMOUS identity = no one knows who they really are.
questions.retry_hint: 'AN' before the blank means the word begins with a vowel sound, and the identity carries NO REAL NAME. Ask: which box word describes someone whose name is unknown? Nobody can recognise a person hiding behind it.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'the ___ age — knowing how to enjoy technology' = digital age.
questions.learning_tip: DIGITAL = relating to computers and electronic technology. The DIGITAL age = the current period in history where computers and the internet are central to life.
questions.retry_hint: The blank sits between 'the' and 'AGE', and the sentence is about ENJOYING TECHNOLOGY and knowing when to put it down. Ask: which box word describes the world of computers and screens? It must be a describing word here.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.trap_type: 'The students' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! The students WERE reminded to protect their passwords. WAS is only for ONE (singular). STUDENTS = more than one → WERE.
questions.retry_hint: The underlined verb belongs to THE STUDENTS - a whole hall of them. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past form or the plural one? Agreement is decided by the subject alone, and by nothing else.

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — no (negative/zero) vs know (to have knowledge)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'no' (zero/negative) when the meaning is 'know' (to have knowledge of something).
questions.learning_tip: KNOW = to have knowledge or information. NO = not any / negative answer. 'You should no how to spot a fake website' → can you say 'to have knowledge how to'? YES → use KNOW. KNOW = knowledge.
questions.retry_hint: The speaker is listing WARNING SIGNS the students must learn - this sentence is about having knowledge, not about refusing. Ask: does the underlined word mean 'not any', or is a silent letter missing from the front of it?

questions.error_type: Spelling — ie/ei confusion (shield: I before E)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'sheild' putting E before I. 'Shield' follows I-before-E: shIEld.
questions.learning_tip: Rule: I before E, except after C! shIEld = I before E ✅. Remember: 'a shIEld in the fIEld' — shIEld and fIEld both have IE. I before E!
questions.retry_hint: 'SHEILD' swaps its two vowels. Ask: which one comes first in this word, the I or the E? The rule is I before E, except after C - the same order as in field, thief and piece.

questions.trap_type: Students write 'immediate' (adjective) after the action verb 'report'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (report), use an ADVERB: report IMMEDIATELY. Rule: verb + adverb (-ly). 'Immediate' describes nouns; 'immediately' describes HOW quickly to report something.
questions.retry_hint: The underlined word tells us HOW SOON students must REPORT suspicious activity - it describes the action, not a thing. Ask: after an action verb, does an adjective belong, or an adverb? Adverbs of manner take an -ly ending.

questions.trap_type: Students write a plain plural and leave out the apostrophe that shows ownership.
questions.learning_tip: The laptops BELONG TO the organisers -> ORGANISERS' laptops (apostrophe after the -s for a plural owner). Singular: organiser's laptop.
questions.retry_hint: The LAPTOPS belong to the ORGANISERS - several people own them. Ask: does a bare -s on the end of a noun ever show ownership? Where must the apostrophe stand when the owners already end in -s?

E.passage: Last week, our school held a Cyber Wellness Day for all primary students. The students was (1) taught how to recognise phishing emails — messages that try to trick you into giving away your personal details. 'You should no (2) the warning signs: strange email addresses, urgent language and requests for your password,' said the speaker. She also explained how a strong password acts like a sheild (3) that protects your accounts from hackers. Students were told to report any suspicious activity immediate (4) to their parents or teachers without waiting to see what happens next. At the end of the session, the organisers (5) laptops were packed away, and many students said they felt more confident about staying safe online.

questions.sentence_a: You use a strong and unique password for each account.
questions.sentence_b: Your personal information will be much safer online.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'As long as'.
questions.model_answer: As long as you use a strong and unique password for each account, your personal information will be much safer online.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'As long as you will use' — adding 'will' in the 'as long as' clause.
questions.learning_tip: AS LONG AS + simple present, simple future. AS LONG AS you USE a strong password, your information WILL BE safer. NEVER 'will' after 'as long as'.
questions.retry_hint: 'AS LONG AS' sets a condition: the second half only holds while the first half is true. Ask: which sentence is the condition, and which is the result? And can a future 'will' ever sit inside the 'as long as' half?

questions.sentence_a: The teacher asked a question.
questions.sentence_b: Do you share your password with anyone?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The teacher asked...'
questions.model_answer: The teacher asked if we shared our passwords with anyone.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'The teacher asked if do we share our password' — keeping question word order. In reported speech, normal word order is used.
questions.learning_tip: YES/NO question → reported speech: ASKED + IF/WHETHER + subject + verb (normal order). 'Do YOU SHARE your password?' → asked IF WE SHARED our passwords. Word order flips to normal. 'Do' disappears.
questions.retry_hint: Sentence B is a yes/no question: 'DO YOU SHARE YOUR PASSWORD WITH ANYONE?' Ask: which little joining word must follow 'asked' when there is no wh-word to lead? And what happens to the helper 'do' in a reported sentence?

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
It started with one message.

Nina received it on the class chat group on a Monday morning: a photo of her, taken at Sports Day, with a caption that made fun of the way she ran. She did not know who sent it — the account used a fake name she did not recognise.

By lunchtime, twelve people laughed at it.

Nina did not go to the canteen that day. She sat at her desk and stared at her pencil case.

Her form teacher, Mrs Tan, noticed. At the end of the day, she asked Nina to stay behind.

'I didn't want to make a fuss,' Nina said.

Mrs Tan sat down across from her. 'Making a fuss,' she said quietly, 'is exactly what we need to do when something like this happens. Not to punish. To fix.'

Nina showed her the screenshot. Mrs Tan took her time looking at it, then nodded.

'This is not a joke,' she said. 'It is not harmless. And it is not going to continue.'

By the next morning, the post was removed and the fake account was reported. Nina did not know what the school said to the students involved. But the laughing stopped.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 2 has the same meaning as 'a short description or title added to a photo'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Account' = a user profile; 'message' = written communication; 'group' = a collection of people. CAPTION = a short description or title added to a photo or image.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: A CAPTION = a short text placed under or over a photo to describe or comment on it. The photo had a CAPTION that made fun of her = a mocking label was placed on the image.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 5, what does 'it' refer to in 'Mrs Tan noticed'?

options.1: The message on the class chat
options.2: That Nina did not go to the canteen and sat alone

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' = the message. But Mrs Tan noticed Nina's behaviour — she was sitting alone at her desk.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: 'Nina did not go to the canteen. She sat at her desk and stared at her pencil case.' Paragraph 5: 'Mrs Tan NOTICED.' She noticed NINA'S BEHAVIOUR — sitting alone, not eating, looking distressed.

mcq_questions.stem: What does Mrs Tan mean when she says 'Not to punish. To fix'?

options.1: She wants to punish the students who laughed.
options.2: She does not believe any punishment is needed.
options.3: She wants to address the situation to stop the harm, not just to get someone in trouble.
options.4: She plans to fix Nina's phone settings.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking Mrs Tan wants revenge. Her statement clarifies that her goal is to stop the harm, not to punish.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 7: 'NOT TO PUNISH. TO FIX.' Mrs Tan is saying: the reason to act is not revenge or punishment — it is to STOP the situation and make things right. She focuses on the OUTCOME, not retribution.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 2, is it True or False that Nina knew who sent the message? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says 'the account had a fake name she did not recognise' — so Nina could not identify who sent the message.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, she saw the message.' She saw it, but she did not know who sent it.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'The ACCOUNT HAD A FAKE NAME she DID NOT RECOGNISE.' Nina could not tell who sent it because the sender used a false identity. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: Why did Nina not go to the canteen at lunchtime?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Nina was upset about the photo and mocking caption on the class chat — twelve people laughed at it, and she did not want to face them in the canteen.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she was not hungry' — the passage implies she was avoiding people, not that she wasn't hungry.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: By lunchtime, TWELVE PEOPLE laughed at the photo. Paragraph 4: 'Nina did not go to the canteen.' She stayed away because she was hurt and likely did not want to face those who laughed.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Tan do after Nina showed her the screenshot? Give TWO details.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) She took her time looking at the screenshot before responding — showing she took it seriously. (ii) She clearly stated that it was not harmless and that it was not going to continue.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she helped Nina' — too vague. The passage gives specific actions and words.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 8: Mrs Tan TOOK HER TIME looking at the screenshot. Paragraph 9: 'This is NOT A JOKE... NOT HARMLESS... NOT GOING TO CONTINUE.' Two specific responses — careful attention and clear decisive statement.

open_ended_questions.stem: What happened to the post and the fake account by the next morning?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: The post was removed and the fake account was reported.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'the problem was solved' — too vague.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: 'the POST WAS REMOVED and the FAKE ACCOUNT WAS REPORTED.' These are two specific outcomes. Both are needed for a complete answer.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her words and actions, describe TWO character traits of Mrs Tan with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) PERCEPTIVE: Mrs Tan noticed Nina was sitting alone and staring at her desk without being told — she spotted that something was wrong just by watching. (ii) DECISIVE: she clearly stated 'it is not going to continue' and by the next morning the post was removed and the account reported — she acted quickly and firmly.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'caring and strict' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: PERCEPTIVE = NOTICED Nina sitting alone, ASKED HER TO STAY BEHIND. DECISIVE = said 'NOT GOING TO CONTINUE' and by NEXT MORNING post removed + account reported. Name trait → give evidence.

questions.stem: The young athlete's determination was as ________ as steel — nothing could shake her belief in her own dream.
questions.trap_type: 'Weak', 'heavy' and 'cold' do not describe the quality of determination. STRONG = having great power, force or resilience.
questions.learning_tip: AS + adj + AS = Simile! Her determination was AS STRONG AS steel = comparing its unbreakable quality to steel. STRONG = having great power and resilience that cannot be bent or broken.
questions.retry_hint: Her determination is measured against STEEL, and NOTHING COULD SHAKE HER BELIEF. Ask: which word describes something that cannot be bent or broken? 'Weak' is its opposite, and 'heavy' and 'cold' describe metal, not willpower.

questions.stem: Great opportunities to follow your dreams come ________, so you must be ready to grab them with both hands when they appear.
questions.trap_type: 'Every day' means frequently; 'out of the blue' = unexpectedly; 'on purpose' = deliberately. ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = very rarely, only once in a long while.
questions.learning_tip: IDIOM: ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = something that happens very rarely, almost never. Opportunities come ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = only very rarely. A 'blue moon' is an extremely rare event — hence the idiom.
questions.retry_hint: If you MUST BE READY TO GRAB THEM WITH BOTH HANDS the moment they appear, such chances must be rare. Ask: which idiom means 'hardly ever'? 'Every day' says the exact opposite, and 'on purpose' means done deliberately.

questions.stem: At the end of each year, the class would ________ their graduation ceremony with great excitement.
questions.trap_type: 'Forget', 'give up on' and 'run away from' all show negative feelings. LOOK FORWARD TO = feel excited and positive about something coming in the future.
questions.learning_tip: PHRASAL VERB: LOOK FORWARD TO = feel excited and positive about something in the future. They LOOKED FORWARD TO graduation = they were excited and happy anticipating it. LOOK + FORWARD + TO work together.
questions.retry_hint: The class feels GREAT EXCITEMENT about a ceremony that is still ahead of them, AT THE END OF EACH YEAR. Ask: which phrasal verb means to await something happily? 'Forget', 'give up on' and 'run away from' all turn away from it.

questions.stem: The young inventor showed great ________ — she turned every failure into a new idea and never stopped trying.
questions.trap_type: 'Silence' = no sound; 'speed' = fast pace; 'caution' = being careful. PERSEVERANCE = continued effort despite difficulty or failure.
questions.learning_tip: PERSEVERANCE = continuing to try despite difficulties or failures. The inventor showed great PERSEVERANCE = she never gave up even when things went wrong. PERSEVERE = keep going; PERSEVERANCE = the quality of doing so.
questions.retry_hint: She TURNED EVERY FAILURE INTO A NEW IDEA and NEVER STOPPED TRYING. Ask: which word names the quality of keeping on despite setbacks? 'Speed', 'silence' and 'caution' say nothing about refusing to quit.

questions.stem: Her dream was to become a scientist who would ________ life-saving medicines for patients around the world.
questions.trap_type: 'Sell' = exchange for money; 'remove' = take away; 'copy' = imitate. DEVELOP = create or produce something new through research and work.
questions.learning_tip: DEVELOP = create, build or produce something new through effort and research. A scientist DEVELOPS new medicines = she creates them through long study and testing.
questions.retry_hint: A scientist does not simply hand out LIFE-SAVING MEDICINES - she must bring them into existence through research. Ask: which verb means to create something new? 'Copy' repeats what exists, and 'remove' takes something away.

questions.stem: No one in the class ________ what they will be doing in twenty years, but everyone has a dream.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'know' thinking 'no one in the class' = many people. NO ONE = singular → verb+S in present tense.
questions.learning_tip: NO ONE / NOBODY / EVERYONE / EACH = Singular! Always use verb+S. No one KNOWS = add -S. 'No one know' is WRONG. Singular indefinite → singular verb in present tense.
questions.retry_hint: The subject is NO ONE, however many classmates sit around. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s? 'No one' behaves like a single person, exactly as 'everyone' does.

questions.stem: Our school has ________ a Young Innovators Award to encourage students who create new ideas.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. 'Establish' is regular: establish → established.
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Our school HAS ESTABLISHED an award = it was created at some point and the award exists now. ESTABLISH → ESTABLISHED (regular verb).
questions.retry_hint: 'HAS' is printed before the blank, so the pair must build a present perfect. Ask: after 'has', do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? This verb is regular, so its ending is predictable.

questions.stem: Kai's model rocket design is the most ________ project our science teacher has ever seen from a Primary Three student.
questions.trap_type: This is a superlative context ('the most ... ever seen') but the blank comes AFTER 'the most' — so we need the base adjective. THE MOST + base adjective = superlative.
questions.learning_tip: THE MOST + base adjective = superlative. The MOST IMPRESSIVE project = the one that impresses more than all others. NEVER 'more impressive' after 'the most'. 'Impressiver' is always WRONG.
questions.retry_hint: Read the words already there: THE MOST. The superlative is built for you, so the blank needs the plain adjective. Ask: may you ever stack 'more' or an -er ending on top of 'the most'? One comparison marker is enough.

questions.stem: The students ________ their graduation speeches when the principal walked into the hall.
questions.trap_type: 'The principal walked in' = sudden interrupting event. Students were already rehearsing = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The principal WALKED IN = sudden past event. Students were already rehearsing = WERE REHEARSING (past continuous). Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress.
questions.retry_hint: THE PRINCIPAL WALKED INTO THE HALL - a sudden arrival that cut across the practice. Ask: which choice shows an action still in progress in the PAST? The speeches were not finished when the door opened.

questions.stem: There is ________ room for doubt in Priya's mind — she knows exactly what she wants to do with her life.
questions.trap_type: 'Room' (for doubt) is uncountable → use LITTLE. 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' are for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: LITTLE + uncountable noun. Room (for doubt) = uncountable → LITTLE room for doubt. 'Few room' is WRONG. LITTLE = not much (for uncountable things).
questions.retry_hint: ROOM FOR DOUBT cannot be counted - there is no such thing as 'two rooms for doubt' - and Priya KNOWS EXACTLY what she wants. Ask: which choice goes with an uncountable noun to mean 'hardly any'? 'Few' and 'many' need countable things.

questions.stem: Chasing your dreams takes courage and hard work, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive present simple ('takes') → negative question tag. 'Takes' (third person singular) → doesn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive simple present (third person singular) → negative tag. Chasing dreams TAKES courage, DOESN'T it? DOES → DOESN'T. POSITIVE → NEGATIVE tag.
questions.retry_hint: The statement is positive and its verb TAKES is a plain present verb - there is no 'is' or 'has' to echo. Ask: which helping verb stands in for a plain present verb, and does a positive statement take a positive tag or a negative one?

questions.stem: The award for the most creative project ________ to a student who designed a water purification device last year.
questions.trap_type: The award received the action. Past passive: was/were + past participle.
questions.learning_tip: WAS/WERE + past participle = passive! The award WAS GIVEN = someone gave it; the award received the action. WAS for singular subject.
questions.retry_hint: THE AWARD cannot hand itself over - the school did that, LAST YEAR. Ask: which choice is passive (the subject receives the action) and set in the past? There is only one award, so the helping verb must be singular.

questions.stem: The careers counsellor asked the students ________ about the subjects that interested them most.
questions.trap_type: Positive reported speech: asked + object + to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: ASKED someone TO + base verb. The counsellor asked students TO THINK about the subjects they liked. Formula: asked + person + to + verb (base form).
questions.retry_hint: ASKED THE STUDENTS = a reported request, and it is about THE SUBJECTS THAT INTERESTED THEM MOST. Ask: after 'asked + person', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? Pick the full infinitive.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb 'dream' — 8 forms)

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Every child (1)________ of making a difference in the world one day.' Signal: 'every child' = singular subject, regular habit = simple present. EVERY = singular → dreams.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dream' (base form) instead of 'dreams' (third person singular present). EVERY child = singular → add -S.
questions.learning_tip: Simple present, singular subject (every child) → add -S. Every child DREAMS = regular present, singular. 'Every child dream' is WRONG. EVERY = singular → dreams.
questions.retry_hint: The subject is EVERY CHILD - one child at a time, even though there are millions of them. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the one wearing -s? Every box entry is the same verb; only the ENDING differs.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She spent all of Saturday (2)________ about what it would be like to live on another planet.' Signal: 'spent... (2)___ing' = gerund after SPEND + time. SPEND + time + verb-ing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to dream' (infinitive) instead of 'dreaming' (gerund after spend + time).
questions.learning_tip: SPEND + time + verb-ING (gerund). She spent Saturday DREAMING = spent time in the activity of dreaming. 'Spent to dream' is WRONG. SPEND + time + -ING.
questions.retry_hint: Look at the words before the blank: SPENT ALL OF SATURDAY. Ask: after 'spend + a length of time', which form of the verb follows - the plain one, the one with 'to' in front, or the one ending in -ing?

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last night, she (3)________ of standing on a stage and accepting a Nobel Prize.' Signal: 'last night' = past tense. DREAM → DREAMED (regular) = simple past.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreamt' (acceptable irregular past) but 'dreamed' is in the word_box.
questions.learning_tip: DREAM in the past = DREAMED (regular) or dreamt (irregular). Both correct, but DREAMED is in the word_box. 'Last night she DREAMED' = simple past. DREAM → DREAMED.
questions.retry_hint: LAST NIGHT is finished time, and nothing cuts across the event - it is over and done with. Ask: which box entry is a simple past form standing alone, with no helping verb beside it? A past continuous always needs a partner.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While she (4)________ about the future, her teacher noticed she was not paying attention to the lesson.' Signal: WHILE + background ongoing past action = past continuous. Singular subject 'she' → WAS DREAMING.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreamed' (simple past) instead of 'was dreaming' (past continuous, ongoing background action). 'While' signals the ongoing background.
questions.learning_tip: 'While she ___' = ongoing past background = past continuous. She WAS DREAMING about the future = she was in the middle of daydreaming. The teacher noticed = the interrupting event.
questions.retry_hint: WHILE opens a long background action, and HER TEACHER NOTICED cuts across it. Ask: which box entry shows one girl in the middle of something in the past? Watch the helping verb - the subject is only SHE.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'All the children in the class (5)________ of different futures when the school bell rang to signal the end of the day.' Signal: plural subject 'all the children' + past continuous (while the bell rang) → WERE DREAMING.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'was dreaming' (singular) instead of 'were dreaming' (plural). All the children = plural → WERE.
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject (all the children) + ongoing past = WERE DREAMING. WAS is for singular; WERE for plural. All the children WERE DREAMING = they were all in the middle of daydreaming.
questions.retry_hint: ALL THE CHILDREN is plural, and THE BELL RANG interrupted them in the middle of something. Ask: which box entry shows a past action still in progress AND carries a plural helping verb? Count the subject before you choose.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'It is never too early (6)________ big, her teacher always said.' Signal: 'It is ... (6)___' = IT + IS + adjective + TO-INFINITIVE structure. TO + base verb = infinitive.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreaming' (gerund) instead of 'to dream' (infinitive after 'too early to').
questions.learning_tip: IT IS [adj] + TO + base verb = infinitive structure. It is never too early TO DREAM = infinitive. 'Too early dreaming' is WRONG. TO + base verb = the infinitive form.
questions.retry_hint: Look at the pattern: IT IS NEVER TOO EARLY ___ BIG. Ask: after 'too early', 'too late' or 'too tired', which form always follows - the one ending in -ing, or the infinitive with its little word in front? Say it aloud.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Her parents always told her to (7)________ big and never give up on what she wanted.' Signal: TOLD HER TO + base verb = infinitive. Base form follows 'to'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreams' or 'dreaming'. The word TO is printed in front of the blank, and only a plain verb can follow it.
questions.learning_tip: TO + base verb = the infinitive. Told her TO DREAM big. After 'to', a verb never carries -s or -ing.
questions.retry_hint: The words TOLD HER TO are already printed in front of the blank. Ask: after the little word 'to', which form of a verb may ever follow - the plain one, the one with -s, or the one with -ing? An infinitive takes no ending.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Many of these children (8)________ of the same future for years to come.' Signal: 'for years to come' = future reference. WILL + base verb = future simple.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dream' (present) instead of 'will dream' (future). 'For years to come' = future.
questions.learning_tip: 'For years to come' = the future. WILL + base verb = simple future. They WILL DREAM of these futures = they are going to dream of them in the future. WILL DREAM = future simple.
questions.retry_hint: FOR YEARS TO COME points ahead, not backwards - none of this has happened yet. Ask: which box entry is set in the FUTURE? A present or past form cannot reach into years that have not arrived.

C.passage: Every child (1)________ of making a difference in the world one day. She spent all of Saturday (2)________ about life on another planet. Last night, she (3)________ of standing on a stage and accepting a Nobel Prize. While she (4)________ about the future, her teacher noticed she was not paying attention. All the children (5)________ of different futures when the bell rang to end the day. It is never too early (6)________ big, the teacher always said. Her parents always told her to (7)________ big and never give up on her goals. Many of these children (8)________ of the same future for years to come.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Everyone has at least one dream for the future. A strong (1)________ — a deep desire to achieve something great — keeps a person going through hard times. Having a (2)________ — someone you look up to — helps greatly. Such a person can (3)________ you to try harder and reach higher. People who follow their dreams (4)________ to improve themselves every day, setting small goals. Finding your true (5)________ — the activity that excites you most — is the first step toward a future you are proud of.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a deep desire to achieve something great — keeps a person going through difficult times' = ambition.
questions.learning_tip: AMBITION = a strong desire to achieve something great. AMBITION is what drives you to keep working when things are hard. An AMBITIOUS person has strong AMBITION.
questions.retry_hint: The dash defines it: A DEEP DESIRE TO ACHIEVE SOMETHING GREAT that KEEPS A PERSON GOING THROUGH HARD TIMES. The blank follows 'a strong', so it must be a noun. Ask: which box word names that inner drive?

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a person you look up to who shows you what is possible through hard work' = role model.
questions.learning_tip: A ROLE MODEL = a person whose behaviour and values others admire and try to copy. A good ROLE MODEL shows you what is possible and motivates you to do better.
questions.retry_hint: The dash explains it: SOMEONE YOU LOOK UP TO. Ask: which box entry names a person you admire and want to copy? The other entries name a feeling, a drive or an action - not a human being.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'to try harder and reach higher than you thought possible' = inspire.
questions.learning_tip: INSPIRE = fill someone with the desire and ability to do something great. A role model INSPIRES you = makes you believe you can do more than you imagined.
questions.retry_hint: SUCH A PERSON makes you TRY HARDER AND REACH HIGHER. The blank follows 'can', so it must be a plain verb. Ask: which box word means to fill someone with the will to do great things?

questions.trap_type: The clue 'to improve themselves every day, setting small goals' = strive (make great efforts).
questions.learning_tip: STRIVE = make great efforts toward a goal. People who follow their dreams STRIVE to improve = they work hard consistently toward something they want.
questions.retry_hint: They IMPROVE THEMSELVES EVERY DAY, SETTING SMALL GOALS. The subject is plural, so the blank must be a plain verb. Ask: which box word means to make a great and steady effort towards a goal?

questions.trap_type: The clue 'the subject or activity that excites you most — first step towards building a future' = passion.
questions.learning_tip: PASSION = a very strong feeling of enthusiasm and love for something. Your true PASSION = the thing that excites you most and makes you feel most alive.
questions.retry_hint: The dash tells you plainly: THE ACTIVITY THAT EXCITES YOU MOST. It follows 'your true', so it must be a noun. Ask: which box word names the thing you love doing above everything else?

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.trap_type: 'The students' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! The students WERE inspired by the speaker. WAS is only for ONE (singular). STUDENTS = more than one → WERE.
questions.retry_hint: Look at who was excited: THE STUDENTS, from the moment she walked in. Ask: is the underlined verb singular or plural, and which one does a plural subject need? Agreement is settled by the subject, nothing else.

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — bare (uncovered/empty) vs bear (to carry/endure)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'bare' (uncovered, empty) when the sentence needs 'bear' (to carry or endure).
questions.learning_tip: BEAR = carry or endure (to bear hardship). BARE = uncovered, empty or plain. 'She could bare the difficulty' → should it be 'endure'? YES → use BEAR. BEAR (endure) ≠ BARE (uncovered).
questions.retry_hint: The sentence is about enduring THE PRESSURE OF TRAINING, not about being uncovered or empty. Ask: which spelling means 'to carry or put up with something'? The same word also names a large furry animal.

questions.error_type: Spelling — ie/ei confusion (brief: I before E)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'breif' putting E before I. 'Brief' follows I-before-E: brIEf.
questions.learning_tip: Rule: I before E, except after C! brIEf = I before E ✅. Remember: 'a brIEf PIE break' — brIEf has IE just like PIE. I before E always in this word!
questions.retry_hint: 'BREIF' has its vowels in the wrong order. Ask: which comes first in this word, the I or the E? Remember: I before E, except after C - the same order as in chief, niece and grief.

questions.trap_type: Students write 'confident' (adjective) after the action verb 'spoke'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (spoke), use an ADVERB: spoke CONFIDENTLY. Rule: verb + adverb (-ly). 'Confident' describes nouns; 'confidently' describes HOW someone speaks.
questions.retry_hint: The underlined word describes HOW the astronaut SPOKE, and it is paired with 'and CLEARLY', which already wears the right ending. Ask: after an action verb, do we need an adjective or an adverb? Make the pair match.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — irregular plural possessive ('children' is already plural, so add 's: children's is CORRECT; 'childrens'' is WRONG)
questions.trap_type: This is a REVERSE error check: 'children's' is the CORRECT form. The error in the passage is 'childrens'' which incorrectly treats 'children' as if it were a regular plural.
questions.learning_tip: CHILDREN = irregular plural (no -s). Possessive: CHILDREN'S (add 's). NOT 'childrens'' — 'childrens' is not a word. CHILDREN'S = belonging to children (irregular plural + 's).
questions.retry_hint: 'CHILDRENS' is not a word: CHILDREN is already plural without any -s. Ask: when a plural does not end in -s, where does the apostrophe go, and what follows it? Compare: the men's team, the women's race.

E.passage: On the last day of school, a guest speaker came to talk to our class about following your dreams. The students was (1) excited from the moment she walked in — she was a real astronaut who spent six months on the International Space Station. She told us there were moments when she could hardly bare (2) the pressure of training, but she kept going because she knew her dream was worth it. She gave a breif (3) overview of life in space before answering questions from the class. When Mei asked her what advice she would give, the astronaut spoke confident (4) and clearly: 'Start with a small goal and build from there.' At the end, we signed the childrens' (5) journal — a book where every student writes down one dream to work toward.

questions.sentence_a: Priya practised her speech every single day.
questions.sentence_b: She became the most confident presenter in the class.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'After'.
questions.model_answer: After practising her speech every single day, Priya became the most confident presenter in the class.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'After Priya practised, she became' — acceptable, but the model uses the more elegant -ing reduction.
questions.learning_tip: AFTER + verb-ing (same subject) = compact and elegant. AFTER PRACTISING her speech every day, Priya BECAME the most confident presenter. Same subject → 'after + -ing' is concise.
questions.retry_hint: 'AFTER' must sit in front of the EARLIER event. Ask: which came first - the daily practice, or becoming the most confident presenter? Both halves share one subject, so the verb after 'after' may take an -ing ending.

questions.sentence_a: The teacher asked Kai a question.
questions.sentence_b: What do you want to be when you grow up?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The teacher asked...'
questions.model_answer: The teacher asked Kai what he wanted to be when he grew up.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'The teacher asked Kai what did he want to be' — keeping question word order. In reported speech, normal word order is used.
questions.learning_tip: WH-question → reported speech: ASKED + WH-word + subject + verb (normal order). 'What DO you WANT to be?' → asked WHAT HE WANTED to be. Word order flips to normal. Do disappears. You → he; grow → grew.
questions.retry_hint: Sentence B is a question aimed at Kai: 'WHAT DO YOU WANT TO BE WHEN YOU GROW UP?' Ask: once it is reported, who does 'you' become, and does the helper 'do' survive? The word 'asked' also pulls the verbs back into the past.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
On the last afternoon of Primary Three, Mrs Chen did something she never did before.

She handed out a strip of paper to every student and told them to write one sentence: what they wanted to be in twenty years.

The room went quiet. Students bent over their papers. Some wrote quickly, as if they always knew. Others stared at the ceiling, tapping their pencils.

Mrs Chen collected the strips without reading them. She sealed them inside a small envelope and taped it to the back of the classroom door.

'I will give this back to you when you finish Primary Six,' she said. 'By then, some of you will have changed your minds. Some of you will have found something new. And a few of you — maybe one or two — will be doing exactly what you wrote today.'

She smiled. 'But all of you — every single one — will be further along than you are now. That is the only thing I can promise you.'

Ahmed kept looking at the envelope after Mrs Chen turned back to the board. He wrote three words: 'help sick people.' He did not know what that would look like yet. But he meant every word.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 3 has the same meaning as 'written or done quickly without hesitation'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Quietly' = without sound; 'sealed' = closed securely; 'stared' = looked fixedly. QUICKLY = done in a short time, without delay or hesitation.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: QUICKLY = done in a short time, without hesitation. Some students wrote QUICKLY = they knew their answer right away and wrote without pausing. QUICK → QUICKLY (adverb).

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 6, what does 'That' refer to in 'That is the only thing I can promise you'?

options.1: That all students will become what they wrote
options.2: That every student will be further along in life than they are now
options.3: That the envelope will be returned in Primary Six
options.4: That one or two students will change their minds

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 3 thinking 'that' = the envelope return. But the promise Mrs Chen makes is about growth — being further along.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 6: 'All of you... will be FURTHER ALONG than you are now. THAT is the only thing I can promise.' THAT = the fact that every student will grow and move forward. Not the envelope — the growth.

mcq_questions.stem: Why did Mrs Chen collect the strips without reading them?

options.1: Because she did not have time to read them that afternoon.
options.2: Because she wanted to preserve each student's private dream without judging it.
options.3: Because the strips were too small to read easily.
options.4: Because she had already read what the students planned to write.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking it was about time. But the gesture is clearly intentional — she seals them to protect the students' personal dreams.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: She collected them WITHOUT READING and SEALED them in an envelope. This is intentional — she preserved each dream privately, without judging or commenting. The dream was for the student, not for her.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 2, is it True or False that Mrs Chen told the students to write about their favourite subject? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. She told them to write 'what they wanted to be in twenty years' — about their future ambitions, not their favourite subject.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, she gave them something to write.' She did, but it was about future ambitions, not favourite subjects.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'what they WANTED TO BE IN TWENTY YEARS.' This is about FUTURE AMBITIONS, not favourite subjects. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Chen do with the strips of paper after collecting them?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She sealed them inside a small envelope and taped it to the back of the classroom door, planning to return it to the students in Primary Six.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she kept them' — too vague. The passage gives two specific details.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: She SEALED them inside a small ENVELOPE and TAPED IT TO THE BACK OF THE CLASSROOM DOOR. Both actions are needed for a complete answer.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Chen promise all the students? Give TWO things she said about what might happen by Primary Six.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) Some students will have changed their minds about what they want to be. (ii) A few students — maybe one or two — will be doing exactly what they wrote that day.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students give only the promise that all will grow — that is the main promise but not the two specific things she mentioned.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 5: (1) 'Some of you will have CHANGED YOUR MINDS.' (2) 'A few of you will be doing EXACTLY WHAT YOU WROTE TODAY.' These are two specific predictions she made — use both.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Ahmed write on his strip of paper, and how did he feel about it?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Ahmed wrote 'help sick people' — three simple words. He did not know exactly what that would look like yet, but he had meant every word.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he wanted to be a doctor' — the passage does not say 'doctor'; it says 'help sick people'.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: Ahmed wrote 'HELP SICK PEOPLE' — exactly three words. He 'DID NOT KNOW WHAT THAT WOULD LOOK LIKE YET' but 'HAD MEANT EVERY WORD.' He was sincere even if unsure of the path.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her words and actions, describe TWO character traits of Mrs Chen with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) THOUGHTFUL: she collected students' strips without reading them and sealed them away — showing she respected each student's private dream. (ii) ENCOURAGING: she promised every single student would be 'further along than you are now' — affirming growth for all, regardless of what they wrote.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'kind and caring' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: THOUGHTFUL = sealed papers WITHOUT READING = respected their privacy. ENCOURAGING = 'ALL OF YOU will be FURTHER ALONG than you are now' — promised growth for every single student. Name trait → give evidence.
